utterances.text: In addition to these parties identifying themselves by name, were you able independently to recognise the voices of the speakers in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise General Krstic's voice based on the fact that you heard General Krstic before on a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, many times before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Harmon, but I think you are putting two questions at the same time. Could you divide it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many times did you hear him before, and whether you recognised him. So please do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to intercepting this conversation, are you able to estimate today how many times you had heard General Krstic before this conversation was intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't give you a number, but many times, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on those many times or several times, on the date that you intercepted this conversation, was the voice of one of the speakers General Krstic, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have any doubt about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me next turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 859, and if that could be distributed. And while this exhibit is being distributed, let me ask you, from Konjuh, were important conversations transmitted to the Superior Command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were they transmitted to the Superior Command; by what means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the operator would take down the conversation from the tape into the notebook, the notebook was given to an operator on a computer who would type in the text and, by standard procedure, would send it on to the database.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take a look, please, at Prosecutor's Exhibit 859, which is the exhibit which was just presented to you, and if you take a look at the B/C/S version, does this, Witness Z, appear to be similar to the types of printouts that were sent from Konjuh to the higher command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the conversation that is mentioned in your notebook reflected in Prosecutor's 859, in the printout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the header on this printout, and you will -- can you identify the location where you had intercepted this conversation? At the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the type of device, the frequency, the participants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you go all the way to the top of the printout itself --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, you mean up in the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location is Konjuh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's a date next to the location, August 2nd, 1995. What does that date signify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: That date signifies the day when it was recorded, typed out and sent on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at what frequency did you intercept this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: The frequency was 245.950 megahertz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity, Witness Z, in my office, to listen to two tapes of the same conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in one of those tapes was the voice of General Krstic louder than the other tape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I can play those -- I can ask that those tapes be played once again, or alternatively, I can ask the witness about having heard each of these tapes and making his conclusions based on having heard the two tapes and furnishing a description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Mr. Harmon, I think that we've already heard them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are able to compare.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So I will not replay those tapes if ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, they are the same tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. I understand. I don't think it is necessary to play them again. But let me hear the viewpoint of the Defence. How does the Defence feel about that, Mr. Visnjic or Mr. Petrusic? As the tapes are the same, do you feel the need to have us hear them again or may we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence considers that there is no need for us to hear the same tapes if the witness has heard them. And quite obviously, this has been borne out by Mr. Harmon, so we may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Harmon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear one tape version of the conversation where General Krstic -- the voice attributed to General Krstic was lower and one conversation where his voice was more audible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, of the two conversations that you heard, the two versions, which of the conversations do you believe was intercepted from Konjuh?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume which one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one do you assume was intercepted from Konjuh?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it was the stronger conversation that was intercepted at Konjuh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the stronger conversation," do you mean the stronger -- I'm focusing on General Krstic's voice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Both were stronger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me then -- could you explain to the Judges why you believe that the stronger conversation, where General Krstic's voice is stronger, may have come from Konjuh as opposed to Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was that Konjuh is about 400 metres higher, a higher elevation feature than Okresanica. That is the basic prerequisite for us to hear better on those wavelengths. The reception is better with those -- at that altitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does a greater altitude give you better reception?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my experience as a radio ham as well, I can conclude that yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are conversations, the same conversations, carried over different frequencies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what significance, if any, does the difference of frequencies have on the ability to hear the participants in a conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would happen that on one frequency the signal is weaker and on the other stronger because the equipment has a bearing capacity. It is a telephone signal and has this bearing capacity, and I think it is about 10 megahertz, the scale. And the difference is always felt, was always felt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we had a witness testify in Court - Dr. French - who analysed the tapes, and his testimony was that after a word at the beginning of a conversation -- at the beginning of the tape, after the word "momenat," there was a click, and the word "halo," "hello," was missing, and then the conversation picked back up and carried through the rest of the conversation. Can you explain to the Judges your practice when you intercepted conversations about putting pause buttons -- depressing the pause button?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The tape recorder was always switched on with the pause button, and you can hear the voice from the tape recorder or you could hear it via the headsets, the earphones, if they were switched into the device. And when we hear a signal, we stop the scanner, that is to say, the device that scans the frequencies, or it stops automatically; depends on how it is set. We then approach the tape recorder and, at the beginning of the conversation, we lift the pause and start recording. But if the operator on the -- connecting the participants, if he needs more time on the switchboard to connect them, or if it is busy, then we depress the pause button again and wait for the real participant to make himself heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did that first because we were able to listen to the tapes again much quicker, and the pause would sometimes take as much as half a minute, depending on the switchboard. And also, we did not have enough tapes, and to be able to get in as many conversations as possible on one tape, that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were the tapes on which these conversations were recorded, they were reel-to-reel tapes, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they reused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say you didn't have enough tapes, was the reason why you were depressing the pause button at certain points in order to conserve space on the tapes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me put a question to you. General Krstic has heard one version of the tape-recorded conversation that we've been talking about, and when he heard the version of the tape-recorded conversation, he indicated that it was a hundred per cent a montage. Let me put that proposition to you. Can you comment about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that that is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Z, my name is Nenad Petrusic. I am the Defence lawyer and I'm going to ask you a few questions. And good afternoon to you, before I go ahead. Exhibit 747, and it is the notebook that you have before you, bearing in mind -- taking a look at the first page -- take a look at the first page of that notebook, that is to say, the page numbered 00804344. It has the date, the 24th of July, 1995, written in in handwriting. Can you determine, looking at that date, within what time period did the conversation take place which was quoted to you by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all events, it was after this particular date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this notebook, can you say for certain at the end of the notebook or in any other part of the notebook, can you say -- can you determine the following date, the next date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have a look?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here the 25th/07, and the page is 00804355. Page 801371261 [as interpreted], 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic, I think there has been a slight mistake. You can confirm that, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To economise with the time, Witness Z, at the end of this notebook, is there a date, the date when the notebook was completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is no date at the end of the notebook when the notebook was completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to find the date, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness Z, in the heading when you did your work as an operator, did you introduce the frequency, the time, and the participants in the conversation? Did you include that in the heading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain if in this conversation in Exhibit 787 we have three undisputed participants - General Krstic, Obrenovic, and Jevdjevic - why then in the heading for this conversation you do not have the name of Major Jevdjevic? Why is it not included?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were the participants when they called up. Jevdjevic appeared later on, so we didn't go back to the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you transcribed the conversation, that is to say when you put it down on paper, did you listen to it again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we would listen to it again and put it down on paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be usual for you to introduce the name of the third participant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't be usual or customary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Z, how long did you monitor these conversations before the 2nd of August, 1995; for how much time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to the location sometime in the spring of 1995. I can't tell you the exact date for these conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more precise? You say in the spring of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the spring could have meant May or June 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up until this particular conversation, can you remember whether you had heard General Krstic, the voice of General Krstic up until this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we heard him a number of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "a number of times"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Krstic would call up on the phone frequently, and there were a lot of conversations, ones that were trivial. He would ring up sometimes and just say that he was calling, that he would introduce himself as General Krstic, and then he would wait for the connection, so we could hear him a number of times. But those conversations were not considered important, so some of them we didn't even put them down on paper because they had no particular substance. He would just call up, wait, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear General Krstic in a previous conversation of any kind talking to -- having this -- a conversation with this type of content or a similar content?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about this content because it was only when I came here that I actually saw this particular conversation, and I don't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first see this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when I came here the first time, when I came to the Prosecutor the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in June last year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, since last June up until a few days ago. I wasn't able to see it again, nor did I ask to see it again, nor did I remember that it existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in June earlier on, you didn't know -- in June 2000 you didn't know of the existence of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had forgot that it existed at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness Z, did you at one time talk to Mrs. Stephanie Frease?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember having had the conversation, but not the actual conversation. We signed some papers, something like that. She asked us to be witnesses, to give our consent because of some things that could ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness Z, that on that occasion the lady that worked for the OTP brought to your attention this conversation, and to that you answered the following: "Then Mr. Z was asked," and I quote, "to leaf through the photocopy of notebook 103 on pages 46, 53 to 55, 64 to 72B, 86 to 89, and to identify his handwriting. After having identified his own handwriting in notebook 103 on page 87 and 88, he was asked to read the transcript. The time of the conversation, 9.50, the frequency, 245.950, and it was between General Krstic and Obrenovic. [redacted] said that he remembers the recording of the conversation from the tape and the exact sentence, and the concrete sentence, `We're working. Yes, we are. Someone gets caught on a mine or a barrel.' The witness recalled that conversation because at that time he knew that in the forest there were a lot of Bosnians who had difficulties in finding the road, the way to the free territory. The witness also confirmed that he had written the word `Wednesday' which appears before the beginning of that particular conversation." Witness Z, are these records done by the OTP correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore on that 21st of November, 1999, you -- this conversation was brought to your attention by the representative of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was brought to my attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that time, as you say, up until two or three days ago, you did not have occasion to either hear or read through the transcript of that conversation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation? Do you know why you were not asked about the contents of that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had no explanation for that, no. At the time when Ms. Stephanie was there, it was just recognition of the handwriting, but the actual matter -- I didn't -- I just simply forgot those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Just a moment, please. We wish to confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, any re-examination? We shall try to finish with this witness prior to the lunch break, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Judge Fouad Riad, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness Z, good morning. You can hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I have just one question, or perhaps one and a half. In one of the conversations which we have just seen, and the Prosecutor's Exhibit 859, there is General Krstic saying, or allegation, "The Turks are probably listening. Let them listen, the motherfuckers." Now, in case -- in such cases, did you ever notice at any point in time that some of these conversations appeared later to be meant to mislead your party since they knew that you were listening, that your party was listening? Did you discover afterwards that they were fake, as sometimes it is done when people know that others are listening? What's your experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, my job was to copy down from the tape and to send it to superiors, because they were the people over there who were to study these things and decide. We didn't give much thought to these things ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And now, you seem to -- you said you had been listening to the frequencies of the voices and you started knowing them. Whenever you heard the voice of General Krstic, did you immediately know that it was him or you waited to know -- to have him announce himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the frequency of his telephone, and if our device stopped at that frequency, we would tape the conversation. If he introduced himself, fine; if he didn't, then we'd take down the frequency and forward it on, and then they would probably know who it was. It was up to us to assume who it was. If we recognised the voice, we would say it was General Krstic; if we were not sure, we would put a question mark. And that is how it was sent on, and then they would summarise these things further from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did it happen at any time that you would point out that it was a certain person and then the experts would find out that it's not the voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: For some persons, for persons that we were not sure of, we would put a question mark. We would never put names down just like that, because we would be lying to ourselves and then to everyone else. That was not our aim. Our aim was to report the information correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald, no questions. Witness Z, I have a few questions. I shall try to be quick. You told the Prosecutor, with respect to the idea of a montage, as expressed by General Krstic, your answer was that that was quite impossible. Why do you say that that was quite impossible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was there, because I know what we were doing. That is one reason. And secondly, I don't think any one of us had sufficient knowledge or skill to make such a montage. It never occurred to anyone. There was a war on. What was important was to listen in, to intercept, and convey the information if it could assist our people. That was our aim. We didn't know that this would happen. If we had known, then we would have acted in an entirely different manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another point: Could you take the notebook - the number I see on it is 103 - and tell us on which page you see the date of the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is indeed page 371 at the end, because the transcript said, 58 -- line 12, on page 58, line 12, that the pages -- that the three last numbers were 261. So it is 371, is that right, the last three numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. A final question from me, Witness Z. You told my colleague, Judge Fouad Riad, that there were brackets that you used as a kind of code, that it had a definite meaning. Did your colleagues apply the same procedure? Did they use the same brackets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Z [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each one of us had his own methods. We never made any agreements. But simply when the operator took down these tapes, he had his own way to mark things that would assist him should anyone ask him about it, so he could give an explanation, and it would be easier for him to take down the recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Witness Z. You have completed your testimony. Thank you very much for coming. I think that Mr. Harmon has some documents to tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise that the Court was going to defer its decision on the admission of these documents, but I would like to move into admission Prosecutor's Exhibit 747, which is a copy of the notebook; 787, which is an excerpt; and 859, which is a printout. And 747 should be under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, there are three exhibits. Is that right, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Petrusic, I think you have the same position as you took with respect to the other exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Defence abides by the objections made earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Chamber also maintains its position, so we will defer the time for deciding on the admission of these exhibits. So now, Witness Z, thank you very much for coming. I'm going to ask the usher to pull the blinds so that you may leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let us have the lunch break now. Can we come back at 2.00? Yes, 2.00. So we'll resume work at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, counsel. Your Honours, the next witness is Witness W. Witness W testified previously with protective measures; face distortion, voice distortion, and a pseudonym. He testified on the 20th and the 26th of June, 2000. I have discussed reimplementing the same protective measures with my colleagues from the Defence, and they have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, no, Mr. President, we have no objection to the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber grants the right to this motion, and the same protective measures will apply as applied earlier. We now have Witness W. Witness W, do you remember being here on the 20th and 26th of June, 2000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You took the solemn declaration at the time, so we consider that you are still under oath, and I'm sure you know what that means. Mr. Harmon, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Harmon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness W.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 855, 856, and 857 distributed to the witness and to the parties and to the Court, then I can proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while I'm waiting for the distribution of these particular exhibits, just to refresh the Court's recollection, when you testified previously, Witness W, you testified that you had formed an interception group that was stationed at Okresanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could put it that way, although I formed it at the initiative or following orders from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your group, your intercept group was associated with the State Security Service and not the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We worked in the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to wait until you receive the exhibits before I continue with my examination. Witness W, could you inspect Prosecutor's Exhibit 855, and when you've finished, just let me know when you've finished inspecting that particular exhibit. Witness W, I'm interested in the conversation on Prosecutor's Exhibit 855 which is numbered 988.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have just seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having inspected this exhibit, Witness W, can you tell from your inspection whether or not this is an intercepted communication that was intercepted by the State Security Service, by your intercept group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document that we did. We intercepted it and compiled it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, in the upper left-hand corner there is a header at the very top left-hand corner that says the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and indicates a date, a location. Do you see what I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you will see a dotted line in the upper third of the conversation, and then you will see below that the initials or the letters CSB-SDB Tuzla, the date, and a number. Can you explain what those two different portions of this document mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's a document which we gave over to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we spoke about this last time. I hope that we don't have to go into the exchange of documents at Okresanica. They took over the document, they recorded it, assigned it a number, and the authenticity of the report compiled by my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, focusing your attention on the portion that says CSB-SDB Tuzla, the date of the August 1st, 1995, and then a number, what does the date represent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the date -- this date represents the time when the conversation took place and the number under which it was registered in the records book, recordkeeping book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So turning your attention to the conversation number 988, on what date was that conversation intercepted? When I say "988," Witness W, I'm still referring to Prosecutor's Exhibit 855.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We can see here that it is one report which was typed into a file, which means that all these conversations, as far as I can see, took place on the same day at different times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if you could turn your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 856. I'm specifically interested in the conversation that is numbered 998. First of all, inspect the document, and when you finish inspecting the document, let me know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've already seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a document that was intercepted by your unit from Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber on what date the conversation that is numbered 998 was intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 1st of August, 1995, and of course at 2245 hours exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention to the last exhibit in this series. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 857. And I'd like you to focus on the conversation number 999.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this intercept as one that was intercepted by your unit from Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's our document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the date of this particular intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a continuation of the other document, the previous document, because it's on the same frequency at such-and-such an hour. We recorded another conversation between these two men again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so would that conversation also have been intercepted on the 1st of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to this, it would be -- that would be it, but I can check it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you check it out here, while you're here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have it with me somewhere in the diary that we kept and where these documents were recorded, registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you check it out, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. You're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will be objecting, but I think the witness will be able to answer. That is to say, is this document that the witness is looking at now his personal document or is it an official document in which he introduced certain data, that is to say, an official document of the service to which he belonged, all as a function of the job he did?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, are you going to ask those questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll be glad to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us finish this question, which is: Can you tell us the date when the conversation that is numbered 999 was intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it here. That is, it says the file, and the file was coded and prepared to be handed over on the 2nd of August, 1995, at 0044 hours, that is to say, after midnight. And it therefore appears that as the conversation was at 2300 hours, that after that we moved on to the next day. So I have it registered that it was coded on the 2nd of August, 1995 and that it was dispatched at 0044 towards the base, dispatched to base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise the formatting in each of these intercepts as being the formatting that was used by your organisation at the time these conversations were intercepted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Everything is as it was recorded by us, the formulation at the beginning of the text and so on, the type of lettering, the type of print, and everything else. And I spoke about that last time. I don't think you'll be needing it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, my colleague raised a question as to whether or not you personally intercepted these conversations. Can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand it to be -- that to be the question. I don't think they asked me that. But of course I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, that hopefully answers my colleague's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, but, Mr. Petrusic, perhaps you could ask that question in the cross-examination, because the question was the nature and the provenance of the document that the witness is using. Your question was along those lines. But I think, Mr. Petrusic, that you could ask those questions yourself when you come to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I completely agree with you, Mr. President, and that is not what we are contesting. What is contested is that if this notebook is a working document, then it has a completely different character, and the Defence attaches a different dimension to it with respect to the further questioning of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll leave that to my colleague to cross-examine on, but I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. Mr. Petrusic, you will have the opportunity now of going ahead with your questions. Ask your own questions. You each have your salaries, so you do your work, Mr. Harmon does his work. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, but none, of course, here are acting solely with our salaries in view. I think that is undisputed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was joking. You're right. We are here to achieve some far more important objectives than that, and thank you for reminding me of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that was not my intention at all, but I accept what you said as a good joke. Cross-examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, my name is Nenad Petrusic. I have several questions for you in connection with your testimony, so let us start with the objection that the Defence made regarding this notebook. The notebook that you just took out of your bag, is it a working notebook that you used while doing your job at the interception centre at Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Records of all dispatches received and sent had to be kept somewhere, and we registered them in this logbook, so it is an official document and not a private one because all documents that were sent from the communication centre, or, rather, from that location were taken note of when they were received and when they were sent out. So this is an official document, not a private one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did my learned friends from the Prosecution or the investigators who interviewed you have a chance to have insight into your notebook when determining the timing of the conversation, or, rather, the timing when it was dispatched to the computer centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't ask me for it. If they had, I would have let them look at it. May I just add, I can't even remember. Perhaps some of the pages were taken from me, because after all, it was a long time ago when we had our conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, when did you start working at this interception centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at Okresanica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the end of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that interception centre, did you have occasion, you personally, to hear General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope you will understand me. I had occasion to hear many people. Among them, he was certainly one of them. But there was a great deal of work to do, and we were very few, so I couldn't tell you now that I heard Krstic or Mladic or anyone else on such and such a day. We listened in. This was really just a technical procedure, to hear, record, reproduce, and forward. So that would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, in your statement dated the 20th and the 26th of June you said, among other things, that the heading or the header that you prepared was of standard format, and the header would include a number, the direction, the frequency, the channel, the time, and the participants in the conversation that was being recorded. Am I right when I say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mostly tried to have the header always contain the same elements. Sometimes it may not have been necessary, as in the case of this document, 999, because it is pointed out that it is a conversation between the same two individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in this document, Exhibit 855, 857, and 856, in the header one of the standard elements that you would register is missing, and that is the direction of the route of the intercepted conversation. Am I right, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you are not. No, no, you're not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Exhibit 855, registered under number 988, your number 988, it says, and I quote, the header, on "Frequency 779.000 megahertz, channel 13, at 1002 hours, we recorded a conversation between Jevtic (J) from Serbia, and Stevo (S) and Ljubija Beara (B) from the Main Staff of the so-called VRS." So in this registered conversation, the route is not indicated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain, the frequency 779 is actually the route. Once we determine that frequency 779 is on the route such and such, it doesn't have to be repeated, though it can be. But in this case the frequency itself determines the route, unless it is replaced with another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness W, I showed you Exhibit 305 to 310 that you testified about in June 2000, but if you can remember now -- but I would like the usher to give you copies of those exhibits. These are exhibits from 305 through to 310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, if I understand you correctly, you would like to show the witness Exhibits 305 up to 310 so that the witness can refresh his memory. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, precisely.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see here the versions in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see A and B, or rather B and C. This is A in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can save time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Witness W, in brief, is that in these exhibits, from 305 to 310, that you testified about, the direction is mentioned in the header. There is indication of the route. However, in these exhibits, 855, 856, and 857, that you testified about today, no such indication is included. Do you have an explanation for that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember which direction frequency 779 - I think it was that we were talking about - had, but maybe it is missing. Maybe it is lacking. But the frequency determined the direction, and we would record it when we knew it. Perhaps in my own log book I could look for it. It may be recorded somewhere which direction corresponds to which frequency, and if you wish me to, I can look it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Fouad Riad? No? Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Could I just ask Mr. Harmon a question? It may be my faulty memory, but have these exhibits, have they -- I know they've been introduced, right, before?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The previous exhibits, I believe, have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I thought. Can you tell me in relation to what? I mean, was it part of the Butler testimony or what? I'm just trying to put it in some kind of context and I'm having trouble.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was in relation to his testimony that he gave on the 20th and 26th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. But that's where -- that's the only place where it came up?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have many exhibits of the same throughout imbedded in the transcript and the Court proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm aware at this point, and I can check in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: No, no, no. I just would ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They came in through Witness W's testimony earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Right. Right. So they're in the book of intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clear up a point. When Mr. Harmon and Madam Judge Wald were talking about these exhibits, you were talking about Exhibits 305 to 310; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Because there are many exhibits here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I was talking about -- I'm sorry. I was talking about, no, the main exhibits: 856, 857, and 858.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I should have given the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: These are new exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- that we're now tendering through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Just tendering them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At this point, and we'll move to admit them at the conclusion of Your Honours' questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Will they ever be sort of tied to the narrative, or we'll take them at their face value, assuming they're admitted, assuming they're admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Initially I asked you to take them at face value. I think Mr. Butler, who was planning to testify later on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- may well be coming in to connect these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I said: Are they going to come up in the -- have they come up or are they going to come up in the Butler testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They may come up in the Butler testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you see, even when speaking the same language, one may be referring to two different things. So before we conclude with the testimony of Witness W, Mr. Petrusic asked you some questions about this direction. At one point you said that if Mr. Petrusic wanted to know the direction, you perhaps had an indication of it in your log book, notebook, or whatever. Can you check that, whether you have taken note of the direction in that log book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. Do you wish me to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, please. Please do that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W: Ferid MUSLIĆ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Could somebody just remind me? Was it 779 or 799? I think it was 779. I have it noted down in the log book. The frequency 836 has its duplex 779, and it is 90 degrees azimuth in relation to the location where we were situated. So as far as I am able to remember, because it really was a long time ago and we have to bear that in mind, that direction was the direction Pale, Han Pijesak, I think Zvornik. I cannot guarantee this a hundred per cent. This is as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very good, Witness. Thank you very much. Mr. Petrusic seemed to be getting on his feet. Do you have any observation to make, Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Witness W, we have no further questions for you. We wish to thank you once again for coming here and we wish you a safe journey home and success in your work. I will ask the usher to accompany you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Harmon. Just a moment, usher. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We would move to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Harmon. I was giving the usher a sign, not to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We would move to enter Prosecutor's Exhibit 855, 856, and 857.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, I see your position is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Defence objects to the admission of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Chamber will take the same position, that is, we will decide when we make a ruling about the other relevant issues relative to this. Witness, please wait a moment for the usher to bring down the blinds. Judge Wald has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have a question. I understand the ongoing dispute about the -- which we will decide tomorrow, about the grounds on which the Prosecutor proposes to admit the intercepts that we discussed the last two days, and specifically they -- one of the grounds is that they are in -- they are collateral evidence to impugn credibility of General Krstic when he actually was on the stand. But I don't understand what link has yet been made about these intercepts being rebuttal evidence since they haven't, to my knowledge, been connected to any testimony of anybody so far, nor do I accept -- from my general knowledge of the case, have an idea what your theory that they're rebuttal, and I know you're going to connect them with Butler later, but he hasn't appeared yet so I don't know whether that connection is a valid one yet. So I'm not sure -- the reason I bring it up, I'm not sure that all of them at this point fall under the same theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree. Perhaps it's premature for me to move these into evidence. They will be connected. These are exhibits that are background evidence to put into context with another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand. Since we're in rebuttal --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Since we're in rebuttal, it does seem to me that the theory of rebuttal as enunciated by the Appellate Chamber here in the recent Celebici case is, you know, there has to be some rebuttal to something that arises out of the Defence case, and as of yet, we don't know that. So I think, at least in my view, I don't have the necessary connecting link to know if I think it is proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think I will withdraw my application for admission at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And do it later. I think that will be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And when these are linked up with -- then we will demonstrate the purpose of the rebuttal, and then I'll move to admit these. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now, yes, you may bring down the blinds, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey will present the next evidence and the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, but perhaps it's only -- it's already ten to three. Perhaps it's not worthwhile beginning now just for ten minutes. I think we will adjourn there now. There's no point in beginning this testimony now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was planning to address an issue that Judge Wald has mentioned in the first five minutes of this testimony. Mr. Harmon and I went slightly out of order with these witnesses because of the order, but I can -- I am prepared to address exactly the issues that she was asking about, and I can do that now, if you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This last witness and the witness that is about to testify are directed -- have been asked to testify to respond to a particular statement made by General Krstic in his cross-examination regarding speaking to Lieutenant Colonel Popovic. He was asked -- now, this was in private session, so to complicate matters, perhaps we should go into private session and I can tell you what the subject matter was, but I don't think it will be something that counsel will be concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let us go into private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that for today, we have no other issues to address, so we will adjourn until tomorrow at 20 past 9. So the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
